memory_candidates.content: When a dispatch file's 'Batch Gate Deferral' section postdates the plan it accompanies, it supersedes a plan phase's own unscoped full-battery-exit-0 verification criterion for THAT dispatch only -- the plan text stays as the standing criterion for future reference, but this dispatch discharges against the scoped substitute instead and records why. Running the unscoped full battery anyway, inside a multi-task /orchestrate batch where sibling implement dispatches are concurrently active and may share declared file_scope (e.g. multiple tasks all declaring verify-deploy.sh and its gate-selection test fixtures), risks a spurious FAIL from either a pre-existing-but-undeclared test-corpus defect or a concurrent-edit race on shared fixtures -- neither of which is this dispatch's regression. Before concluding a full-battery FAIL is a real regression, check for an open tracking task describing the same failing suites as pre-existing (grep specs/ for the suite names), and check whether other agents declared in this session are concurrently touching the same file_scope.

Editing a source-store file ahead of its redeploy intentionally and predictably produces a transient 'deployed script/doc content drift' gate-3 FINDING for that exact file in any differential --findings comparison run before the redeploy -- this is not a regression, it is the expected mid-task signature of the source-store/deployed-tree split itself. The finding (and any Rule R line_count mismatch from an edited markdown file) clears on its own once the redeploy runs. Do not gate an intermediate phase's verification on a differential-findings diff staying perfectly clean when later phases of the same task still owe a redeploy; gate on it only at the final, post-redeploy comparison.
